recentItems.title: The Hunters: Inside NATO's Anti-Submarine Warfare | Submarine Documentary
recentItems.description:
The scariest weapon facing NATO Allies isn’t necessarily an elite Special Forces operator, nor a stealth fighter: it’s a submarine cruising beneath the ocean’s surface, hidden from view, carrying a belly full of torpedoes and ballistic missiles.

Between their stealth and their firepower, submarines present a uniquely serious threat to NATO’s security. But Allies have an answer: a combination of sub-hunting ships, helicopters and maritime patrol aircraft that use sonar sensors to find submarines, and if necessary, neutralise them.

NATO Allies train to hunt subs three times a year. Each body of water has its own unique characteristics, so Allies need to stay ready to tackle threats wherever they might surface. 

This video peeks inside exercise Dynamic Manta 26, hosted by NATO Allied Maritime Command and the Italian Navy in the Mediterranean Sea. Follow along as Allied ships and aircraft try to pin down submarines lurking in the depths below.

recentItems.title: Denmark’s Conscription Is Changing |🇩🇰 From Civilian to Soldier
recentItems.description:
Denmark’s conscription system is changing. Watch Danish conscripts train to become soldiers during the Royal Life Guards’ demanding final field exercise.

Denmark is expanding its conscription system to include women, increasing the annual intake to 7,500 by 2033, and extending standard service from four to 11 months.

This film follows young men and women as they face physical and mental challenges, including field training, night movement, obstacle courses, ration preparation, and the final test known as REX-TUREN.

The transformation from civilian to soldier is part of a wider effort to strengthen Denmark’s national defence and NATO’s collective defence.

Learn more about Danish conscription, Forsvarets Dag, the Royal Life Guards, military training, and NATO readiness.
